remedy.justification: net 'VPWR' exceeds the antenna-ratio limit at 'li1' (ratio 832 > 75); no adjacent stackup level has margin to absorb the excess routing (a layer-local violation with no jump target) -- insert an antenna diode on this net at 'li1' to bleed off accumulated charge

ties_disclosure.reason: No ties[] is declared, so erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED for this layout -- an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. sky130 taps ARE nameable here (tap.drawing 65/44 inside nwell.drawing 64/20, wired to li1 through licon1 66/44), so this is not an unexpressible stream; the obstacle is klayout-tools#2169, whose unisolated tie extraction collapses a real routed standard-cell design into one electrical island and reports a FALSE erc.supply_short from a correct ties[] declaration. Declaring ties[] here would therefore replace a stated gap with a misleading finding. Standing in for the ungraded check, and named so a reader can go look rather than take this on faith: (a) the two std-cell macros are tapped by klt place-and-route's own tap cells -- sky130_fd_sc_hd__tapvpwrvgnd_1 instances are present in the graded GDS by name (text.drawing 83/44 carries 'tapvpwrvgnd_1'), and 12 tap.drawing 65/44 shapes are drawn; (b) the body/tub labels VPB (nwell.label 64/5) and VNB (pwell.label 64/59) are drawn on the wells themselves; (c) the same record's LVS report (lvs.json) carries the supply nets in its net_correspondence -- VDD<->VDD (pin), and ONE digital rail, VPB|VPWR<->VPWR (pin), where issue #344's run saw a split VPWR<->VPWR_SEQ / VPWR$1<->VPWR_SELN pair, because issue #355 made the two std-cell macros' rails one net. NOTE that (c) is a partial standin only: that LVS run's own status is 'mismatch', not 'match', and neither GND nor VGND appears in its net_correspondence at all -- GND appears on the reference side of a net.merged mismatch instead, since GND and VGND extract as the single net GND|VGND.
